title: Taiwan: A Growing Economic Partner for the E.U. in Troubled Times
gist: An op-ed excerpt argues that Taiwan has become a more important EU partner than at any point in the 41 years since EU-PRC diplomatic relations, driven by Europe's push to diversify semiconductor supply chains amid waning confidence in US protection after conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East.

themes.theme: Eroding European reliance on the US

insights.claim: Armed conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East have shocked Europeans into recognizing they can no longer fully rely on close US protection, despite the US remaining NATO's largest military power.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: A structural loosening of the transatlantic security guarantee pushes the EU toward new Indo-Pacific partners, reshaping defense and supply-chain alignments investors track.
insights.quote: armed conflicts in Ukraine and in the Middle East have shocked Europeans who know they can no longer fully rely on the close protection of their traditional ally, the United States

insights.claim: Washington's recent signals have brought confusion to Europe, prompting Europeans to reassess dependence on the United States even as it stays NATO's dominant military power.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Perceived US unreliability is the causal driver behind EU diversification moves; watch for accelerated EU-Asia trade and tech deals as a downstream effect.
insights.quote: Washington’s recent signs and messages have brought confusion to Europe
insights.locator: Although the U.S. remains NATO’s largest military power

insights.claim: Japan and South Korea are now looking at diversification options as East Asia faces a security situation similar to Europe's uncertainty about US commitments.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Parallel hedging by Japan and South Korea signals a broader multi-region realignment away from single-ally dependence, a theme for defense and trade positioning.
insights.locator: In some ways, East Asia faces a similar situation

insights.claim: The EU launched its Indo-Pacific strategy in September 2021 and has since developed multiple ties with Japan, India, South Korea, and ASEAN as it pivots toward Asia.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: The EU's Asia pivot is an established multi-year policy vector; map which Asian economies capture the resulting trade and investment flows.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, the EU is trying to “pivot” toward Asia

insights.claim: Taiwan is the world's premier producer of high-end semiconductors, making its comparative advantages increasingly aligned with European interests as Europe seeks to diversify supply chains and reduce vulnerabilities in strategic sectors.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Taiwan's chip primacy is the core reason it is being pulled into EU strategic planning; a lever for Europe-Taiwan tech and investment deals.
insights.quote: Taiwan remains a special case due to its unique situation as the world’s premier producer of high-end semiconductors
insights.locator: In that context, Taiwan remains a special case

insights.claim: Taiwan has emerged as a significantly more important EU partner than at any point since EU-PRC diplomatic relations were established 41 years ago.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: A historic high in EU-Taiwan alignment, despite the One China constraint, flags rising political room for cooperation that could unsettle EU-China relations.
insights.quote: Taiwan has emerged as a significantly more important partner for the EU than at any previous point since diplomatic relations between the EU and the People’s Republic of China were established, 41 years ago

insights.claim: Once viewed mainly as a trading partner constrained by the EU's One China policy, Taiwan is now being incorporated into European discussions on semiconductor resilience, critical technologies, cybersecurity, digital governance, and Indo-Pacific stability.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Taiwan's move from pure trade partner to strategic-tech interlocutor broadens the surface area for EU-Taiwan cooperation across chips, cyber, and digital governance.
insights.quote: Taiwan has increasingly been incorporated into European discussions on semiconductor resilience, critical technologies, cybersecurity, digital governance, and Indo-Pacific stability
insights.locator: Once viewed primarily as a trading partner
